subject: Renewal: term adjustment & burst fallback plan for Dedicated pool
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@orchidapps.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: term adjustment & burst fallback plan for Dedicated pool

Hi Sophie —

As Orchid Apps approaches renewal next month, I wanted to summarize the options we discussed on the call and propose a simple decision path so we can lock in capacity before your q2 launch. High level: you asked for an additional reserved pool and clarity on what happens when traffic exceeds the committed GPUs.

Proposal (attached: 2027-04-02_Redwood_Proposal_Orchid_Apps.pdf):
- Reserved expansion: add 8x A100-equivalent GPUs to your existing Dedicated pool (net increase from 16 -> 24).
- Throughput guarantee: baseline 200 requests/sec sustained per pool with a 99th percentile latency SLO of 180ms for text-gen workloads over the 24-month term.
- Burst/overflow options (pick one):
  1) On-demand spillover (soft cap): traffic spills to hosted capacity when committed pool is saturated. Pay-as-you-go pricing at 1.8x base token rate. No hard request rejections.
  2) Hard cap: requests above the cap return 429; lower cost on committed pool but no spillover guarantees.
  3) Hybrid credit model: pre-purchase burst credits (e.g., 200M tokens/month) for predictable burst pricing; overflow beyond credits uses on-demand at 1.5x.

Term/price flex: we can offer a 12-month renewal at +6.5% list for the extra GPUs, or a 24-month commit with a 9% overall discount and a 2-month credit applied towards burst usage.

Next steps I suggest: you confirm preferred burst policy (1/2/3) and term (12/24) and we'll provide an updated SOW + SLA addendum.

(attachment: 2027-04-02_Redwood_Proposal_Orchid_Apps.pdf)

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(r) 415-555-0119 | rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@orchidapps.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal: term adjustment & burst fallback plan for Dedicated pool

Rishi —

Thanks for the clean summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: we are excited about the extra GPUs but worried about uncontrolled spend during marketing spikes. A couple of questions: 

1) For the on-demand spillover option, can you provide a sample monthly bill estimate if we have two 6-hour spikes in a month that double token usage? I need a realistic number to show procurement.
2) For the hybrid credit model, how do unused burst credits roll over (if at all)?
3) If we do the 24-month term with discount, can we get a performance SLA credit trigger (e.g., violation > 3x in a quarter triggers a 3% invoice credit)?

Procurement (procurement@orchidapps.com) — feel free to share any additional legal/finance constraints.

Sophie Turner
Head of Product, Orchid Apps
sophie.turner@orchidapps.com
(attachment: internal-notes.txt)

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 11:02 AM Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@orchidapps.com> wrote:
> Rishi —
> 
> Thanks for the clean summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: we are excited about the extra GPUs but worried about uncontrolled spend during marketing spikes. A couple of questions: 
> 
> 1) For the on-demand spillover option, can you provide a sample monthly bill estimate if we have two 6-hour spikes in a month that double token usage? I need a realistic number to show procurement.
> 2) For the hybrid credit model, how do unused burst credits roll over (if at all)?
> 3) If we do the 24-month term with discount, can we get a performance SLA credit trigger (e.g., violation > 3x in a quarter triggers a 3% invoice credit)?

Sophie — good questions. Quick answers below; attaching an SLA addendum draft with the credit language (SLA_Addendum_Burst_Policies_v1.docx).

- On-demand spillover sample: assuming your baseline month uses 4B tokens and a spike doubles token consumption for 12 hours total (two 6-hour spikes), rough incremental cost = ~0.18 * baseline monthly invoice (we modeled token mix and sustained latency in the attached proposal). I can produce a line-item estimate if you share last-quarter usage CSV.

- Credits rollover: for the hybrid model we can offer a 3-month roll-forward window for unused burst credits (applies to credit packages purchased at the start of each billing quarter). After 3 months, unused credits expire.

- SLA credit trigger: yes—Redwood can add a 3% invoice credit if the 99th percentile latency exceeds the SLO by >3x for two consecutive weeks within a quarter. The SLA addendum has the exact measuring windows and sample size.

Internal note for Marissa & Dev (copied):
- Marissa: if they pick 24-month with discount, finance needs the revised invoicing schedule (apply 2-month credit at T+1).
- Dev: can you confirm the practical limits of soft cap routing and expected tail latency when spillover goes to hosted? We should confirm token-rate ceilings per-hosted node.

(attachment: SLA_Addendum_Burst_Policies_v1.docx)

I'll build a toy estimate for Sophie's spike scenario if she can share a CSV. If procurement prefers a hard cap we can reflect the lower ARR in the updated SOW.

Thanks,
Rishi

Rishi —

Thanks for the clarifications and the draft SLA addendum. After reviewing with finance, Orchid Apps prefers the hybrid credit model (option 3) to cap predictable exposure while allowing occasional bursts. We will take the 24-month term to secure pricing and apply the 2-month credit.

Action items for Redwood: 
- Send updated SOW + line-item estimate for the sample spike scenario (I will follow up with a usage CSV tonight).
- Include the SLA credit trigger language in the final DocuSign package.
- Provide DocuSign link and expected timeline for signature (we'd like to complete sign-off by Apr 12).

We'll route the final DocuSign to procurement once the numbers are in.

Sophie Turner
Head of Product, Orchid Apps
